title: Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for pantothenic acid
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (question EFSA-Q-2011-01219).
result: Pantothenic acid is a component of coenzyme A and acyl-carrier proteins and serves in acyl-group activation and transfer. It is ubiquitous in foods and dietary deficiency is rare; deficiency symptoms, including mood changes and sleep, neurological, cardiac and gastrointestinal disturbances, have been described in subjects on a pantothenic acid antagonist and/or a pantothenic acid-deficient diet.
